results.title: Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.
results.description:
Expected after India’s Ladakh naming, the FM’s trade-barrier callouts & tighter FDI PN3 scrutiny for China.

Chinese are posturing. Beijing rarely imposes permanent bans; expect waivers. Licensing bottlenecks create uncertain lead times for Indian EPC contractors pricing Chinese equip—next 'case-by-case' waivers may force contractors to disclose precise project locations & site data to MOFCOM to prove "non-military" use.

Bottomline: suit up & invest—or suck up and stop the border posturing without sufficient leverage.

results.title: A few thoughts on China's export controls, which have been and will continue to be primarily targeted towards India.
results.description:
A few thoughts on China's export controls, which have been and will continue to be primarily targeted towards India. 
1. It shouldn't come as a surprise. China will want to protect its moat from the one large developing economy that can build at scale. 
2. Exports are critical to the Chinese economy, especially when the domestic consumption economy may be struggling. 
3. Given 1 & 2, what are we going to do remains the central question. We have two options imo and we must utilise both: attracting OEMs to set up manufacturing in India & simultaneously develop our own ecosystem. We are terrible at the latter. 
4. Our focus must switch to manufacturing inputs and intermediates, not just the end product. Enough with declaring assembly wins. Let's aim to make or process most things that go in a product. 
5. While we go about working on 4, securing supply chains for inputs/materials we don't have resources for is essentially do or die. This is where govt policy and hard-headed behaviour must kick in. Secure supply by hook or crook. 

We have failed so far because we have been let down by policy and the political economy. Now the political economy evolves as we move towards middle income, but there is no substitute for a hard-headed industrial policy. Everything downstream can be solved.

results.title: Thailand spent years courting Chinese EV makers to build plants there, and now it's worried about the jobs tied to Japanese carmakers.
results.description: Thailand spent years courting Chinese EV makers to build plants there, and now it's worried about the jobs tied to Japanese carmakers. India has kept a tighter gate since 2020, when Press Note 3 put every investment from a country sharing a land border with India through government approval. I think the Thai experience is worth studying closely before anyone here loosens that, because the factory jobs are the part you can't easily get back.
